# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.

## Writing Instructions

The instructions you give to each subagent SHOULD be a smaller piece of the instructions you were given. Do not delegate your full task to a subagent. Subagents do not have access to the information you have retrieved in prior turns or your thoughts. You must provide each subagent with the necessary context it needs in its instructions.

Your instructions to a subagent can be long, up to about 5000 characters. Each subagent is as capable as you are, but starts with a blank slate, so you must provide it specific and detailed information in its instructions.

Examples of poor instructions:
- Analyze the retrieved page to find the number of stations.
- Implement the `dfs()` function.
- Use the article to list the subway connections.
- Prove Lemma 3.
- Continue searching for the magic number.

[Gloria Stuart](Gloria_Stuart "Gloria Stuart") (July 4, 1910 – September 26, 2010) was an American film actress whose career spanned over 70 years. She made her feature film debut in *[Street of Women](Street_of_Women "Street of Women")* (1932), before signing a contract with [Universal Pictures](Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"). She appeared in numerous [Pre-code era](Pre-Code_Hollywood "Pre-Code Hollywood") films for the studio, including the horror comedy *[The Old Dark House](The_Old_Dark_House_(1932_film) "The Old Dark House (1932 film)")* (1932), and the drama *[Laughter in Hell](Laughter_in_Hell "Laughter in Hell")* (1933). She starred as Flora Cranley in *[The Invisible Man](The_Invisible_Man_(1933_film) "The Invisible Man (1933 film)")* (1933), which garnered her widespread fame, and later starred in two films opposite [Shirley Temple](Shirley_Temple "Shirley Temple"): *[Poor Little Rich Girl](Poor_Little_Rich_Girl_(1936_film) "Poor Little Rich Girl (1936 film)")* (1936), and *[Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm](Rebecca_of_Sunnybrook_Farm_(1938_film) "Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (1938 film)")* (1938), both for [20th Century Fox](20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"). She subsequently co-starred in *[The Three Musketeers](The_Three_Musketeers_(1939_film) "The Three Musketeers (1939 film)")* (1939) opposite [Don Ameche](Don_Ameche "Don Ameche").

Dissatisfied with her career in film, Stuart shifted her focus to stage acting. Between 1940 and 1942, Stuart appeared in numerous summer stock plays in [New England](New_England "New England"), including a 1940 production of *[Our Town](Our_Town "Our Town")* in which she starred alongside its playwright and director, [Thornton Wilder](Thornton_Wilder "Thornton Wilder"). By the mid-1940s, Stuart was dedicating her time to the pursuit of various visual arts, including painting, printmaking, [serigraphy](Serigraphy "Serigraphy"), <Bonsai>, and [découpage](D%C3%A9coupage "Découpage"). She gradually returned to acting in the 1970s after a decades-long career as an artist, appearing in minor roles in such films as [Richard Benjamin](Richard_Benjamin "Richard Benjamin")'s *[My Favorite Year](My_Favorite_Year "My Favorite Year")* (1982) and *[Wildcats](Wildcats_(film) "Wildcats (film)")* (1986).

Stuart was cast as 101-year-old Rose Calvert in [James Cameron](James_Cameron "James Cameron")'s drama *[Titanic](Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* (1997), which earned her international notoriety, as well as numerous accolades, including an [Academy Award](Academy_Award "Academy Award") nomination for [Best Supporting Actress](Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress"); which as of 2021, she remains the oldest nominee for the category. The case was set for trial in Los Angeles Superior Court in March 2022.[[32]](Bill_Paxton#cite_note-32)

In February 2022, Paxton's family reached a partial settlement with General Anesthesia Specialists Partnership for $1 million.[[33]](Bill_Paxton#cite_note-33) In August 2022, the case was settled against Cedars-Sinai and Dr. Khoynezhad under undisclosed terms.[[34]](Bill_Paxton#cite_note-34)

**No, Bill Paxton never received any Academy Award (Oscar) nominations.**

Throughout his career, he was nominated for numerous other prestigious awards, including:

**Frances Fisher** (born May 11, 1952) is an American actress. She began her career in theatre and later starred as record executive Suzette 'Red' Saxon in the CBS daytime soap opera *[The Edge of Night](The_Edge_of_Night "The Edge of Night")* (1955). In film, she is known for her roles in *<Unforgiven>* (1992), *[Titanic](Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* (1997), *[True Crime](True_Crime_(1999_film) "True Crime (1999 film)")* (1999), *[House of Sand and Fog](House_of_Sand_and_Fog_(film) "House of Sand and Fog (film)")* (2003), *[Laws of Attraction](Laws_of_Attraction "Laws of Attraction")* (2004), *[The Kingdom](The_Kingdom_(film) "The Kingdom (film)")* (2007), *[In the Valley of Elah](In_the_Valley_of_Elah "In the Valley of Elah")* (2007), *[Jolene](Jolene_(film) "Jolene (film)")* (2008), *[The Lincoln Lawyer](The_Lincoln_Lawyer_(film) "The Lincoln Lawyer (film)")* (2011), and *[The Host](The_Host_(2013_film) "The Host (2013 film)")* (2013). From 2014 to 2015, Fisher starred in the ABC drama series *[Resurrection](Resurrection_(U.S._TV_series) "Resurrection (U.S. TV series)")*. In 2019, she starred in the <HBO> television series [*Watchmen*](Watchmen_(TV_series) "Watchmen (TV series)"), a sequel to the [graphic novel](Graphic_novel "Graphic novel") [of the same name](Watchmen "Watchmen").

## Early life and education

Fisher was born on May 11, 1952, in [Milford on Sea](Milford_on_Sea "Milford on Sea"),[[1]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-1) the daughter of American parents Olga Rosine (née Moen), a housewife, and William Irving "Bill" Fisher, Sr, an oil refinery construction superintendent. Her father was of Russian-Jewish and Hungarian-Jewish descent,[[2]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-2) whereas her mother was of Norwegian ancestry.[[3]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-3) Before she reached the age of fifteen, she had moved nine times and travelled because of her father's job, going to places including Italy, Turkey, Colombia, France, Canada, and Brazil.[[4]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-NYTimes-4)[[5]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-LATimes-5)[[6]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-6)

When she was 15, her mother died and she took on the responsibility of raising her younger brother.[[5]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-LATimes-5) She completed her high school at Lutcher Stark High School in [Orange, Texas](Orange%2C_Texas "Orange, Texas"), where she performed in theatre productions, and later worked as a secretary.[[7]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-tvg-7)

## Career

### Theatre

Deciding to follow her interest in theatre, she moved to New York City, where she subsequently enjoyed a 14-year stage career in regional and off-Broadway productions. She became involved with the [Actors Studio](Actors_Studio "Actors Studio"), where she studied with [Lee Strasberg](Lee_Strasberg "Lee Strasberg").[[4]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-NYTimes-4) Fisher moved to [Abingdon, Virginia](Abingdon%2C_Virginia "Abingdon, Virginia"), where she began her acting career at the [Barter Theatre](Barter_Theatre "Barter Theatre"), a year-round repertory theatre.

During the next 10 years, she concentrated on theatre in New York City and in regional theaters around the East Coast. She has also returned to theatre; she appeared in [Arthur Miller](Arthur_Miller "Arthur Miller")'s last play, *[Finishing the Picture](Finishing_the_Picture "Finishing the Picture"),* produced at the [Goodman Theatre](Goodman_Theatre "Goodman Theatre") in Chicago and in a 2006 production of *[The Cherry Orchard](The_Cherry_Orchard "The Cherry Orchard")* at the [Mark Taper Forum](Mark_Taper_Forum "Mark Taper Forum") in Los Angeles.

In 2019, she starred in the [Laguna Playhouse](Laguna_Playhouse "Laguna Playhouse") production of *[The Lion in Winter](The_Lion_in_Winter "The Lion in Winter")* with [Gregory Harrison](Gregory_Harrison "Gregory Harrison").[[8]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-8)[[9]](Frances_Fisher#cite_note-9)

### Television
